title: stale-token-slice-reclamation-and-client-abandonment-handling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: When clients disconnect or time out while a generation is in-flight we currently create lingering token/KV slices and resume tokens that increase memory and storage pressure on runtime nodes. This ticket implements a lease-based reclamation system for 'stale token slices' (small contiguous ranges of generated tokens / KV cache prefixes) plus a safe cleanup protocol that minimizes impact to resume semantics, tool calls, and structured outputs.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can detect abandoned in-flight token slices per-session within configurable abort_grace_period (default 30s) and mark them tombstoned
GC worker reclaims tombstoned token slices and associated ephemeral KV cache by tombstone_ttl (default 5m) without blocking active generations
Resume API returns deterministic failure mode for reclaimed slices (clear error type) so SDKs can surface appropriate UX
No measurable increase (>1%) in 99th percentile generation latency for steady-state traffic after feature enabled
Prometheus metrics exposed: abandoned_streams_total, reclaimed_token_slices_total, tombstone_count, last_reclaim_duration
End-to-end tests simulate abrupt disconnect + reconnect and verify resume token either succeeds (if not reclaimed) or returns documented reclaim error
design_notes: Use a short-lived lease on stream ownership (lease epoch + renewal heartbeat). If lease expires, the stream is marked 'abandoned' but not immediately deleted — we write a tombstone marker with epoch and reason.
Introduce token-slice metadata with owner_epoch and optional resume_token_id. Tombstone semantics: tombstone_ts, tombstone_by, tombstone_epoch.
GC worker will run async per-node and reclaim tombstoned slices after tombstone_ttl. Reclamation is idempotent and will emit events for auditing.

To preserve structured-output atomicity (function/tool calls), we only reclaim slices for generations that have no pending tool-call acknowledgements and where structured-output finalizer is not outstanding. If a generation is mid-tool-call, extend tombstone_ttl by structured_call_grace.

Tradeoffs: immediate reclamation reduces memory quickly but loses resume surface for legitimate slow clients. Deferred reclamation preserves resume but increases resource use. Default strategy: short grace period + conservative extension if in-progress toolcall/ack.
Cross-tenant safety: reclamation only manipulates ephemeral per-tenant blobs and honors tenant quota. Admins can configure per-tenant tombstone_ttl via tenant config API.
Compatibility: SDKs should map reclaim error to a dedicated enum (ReclaimExpired) so callers can decide to retry a fresh generation or surface a helpful UX.
Instrumentation: add tracing spans for lease_acquire, lease_renew, tombstone_write, gc_scan, reclaim_slice to correlate with noisy tenants and regression hunting.
Feature flag: runtime.garbage_collect.abandoned_streams boolean and runtime.tombstone_ttl override for rollout testing.
Open question: whether to snapshot prefix cache to a cheap disk-based cold store pre-reclaim to improve UX for long-running resume — deferred to follow-up ticket.
implementation_tasks: stream-coordinator: add lease epoch and heartbeat endpoints; update stream open/close protocol (ENG-210111-1)
lease-manager: implement lease expiry hook that writes tombstone metadata to stream-index (ENG-210111-2)
gc-worker: implement tombstone scanner + reclaimer; reclamation must be rate-limited and observable (ENG-210111-3)
kv-cache: add safe-delete API that removes ephemeral prefixes only when no active references exist (ENG-210111-4)
sdk: add ReclaimExpired enum and update streaming client to surface explicit error and guidance (ENG-210111-5)
console: small UX copy for 'Reclaimed session' error in debug logs and Troubleshoot KB (ENG-210111-6)
e2e harness: extend chaos test to simulate abrupt TCP close, SIGKILL client, and intermittent resumes (ENG-210111-7)
add rollout feature flag and config knobs (ENG-210111-9)
testing_steps: Unit tests for lease expiry and tombstone marker semantics
Integration test: start generation, drop client socket, assert tombstone written within abort_grace_period
Integration test: tombstone TTL expiry triggers reclaim and ephemeral KV removal; verify no live generations affected
Chaos test: 1000 concurrent streams with randomized disconnects and tool calls; ensure reclaim throughput keeps memory usage within expected bounds
Compatibility test: SDK resume flow when reclaim happens returns ReclaimExpired and client chooses fresh generation path
Performance regression test: compare 99p latency and p95/p50 token throughput between flag on and off under load
Security review: ensure tombstone metadata contains no PII and audit logs are recorded for reclaimed slices
rollout_steps: Enable feature flag in staging; run full CI + chaos suite; validate metrics and no regressions
Canary: enable on dedicated canary pool (5% of runtime capacity) for 48h; monitor abandoned_streams_total and reclaim error rates
Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over one week if no regressions; rollback if reclaim errors >0.5% of streaming requests or 99p latency increases by >1.5%
Post-rollout: run tenant-level audit to ensure no unintentional cross-tenant reclaim; add runbook entry for manual reclamation and emergency rollback
Follow-up: create ticket to expose tenant tombstone_ttl controls in Console and to evaluate cold-store snapshot option
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Patel: Triage notes — this is causing elevated memory on runtime nodes during rush-hour tests. Prior incidents show ~7% memory leak attributable to abandoned in-flight slices.

2025-02-12 Tomás Berg: Architecture review — leaning to lease+ tombstone pattern. Draft PR for stream-index schema change: /pull/PR-1295 (WIP). Need to confirm tombstone race assumptions with KV cache team.
2025-02-14 Maria Nguyen (KV team): Reviewed — KV safe-delete API must be idempotent; suggested adding a reference counter to prefix metadata. Concern: refcount updates could be hot on large streams.
2025-02-18 Security: Confirmed tombstone metadata does not include prompt contents or user PII. Audit events must be emitted for every reclaim with tenant id + stream id.
2025-02-21 Tomás Berg: Implementation PR opened /pull/PR-1321 — includes lease manager and tombstone writes. Feedback requested on tombstone_ttl default (set to 5m for now).
2025-02-25 QA: Started chaos tests in staging. Found race where structured-tool-call extension wasn't honored; fixed in PR-1329.
2025-02-28 Ops: Added Prometheus metrics and dashboard tile. Observed reclaimed_token_slices_total rising during synthetic disconnect tests. No latency regressions observed.
2025-03-01 Aisha Patel: Merging mainline after QA sign-off. Next: canary rollout to dedicated pool tomorrow and monitor for 72h before full ramp.
